description: Lossless bounded block. Decode every {$ref:N} from shared_values[N] (fully expanded, one lookup). quote_span_table rows: [start,end,original_quote_type,original_quote_metadata]. Each SAME-entry attached_verbatim_passage_spans_ids and answer_quotation_spans_ids references table rows in order; exact quote is full supplied summary[start:end], Unicode half-open. Original object/string metadata retained; __transport_text_field__ names text/verbatim field, remove it on restoration. Span sha256_utf8 reconstructs as SHA256 of exact quote. answer_transport joins restored answer_quotations. All original raw fields/quotes/numeric/case fields reconstruct exactly. No keys or answers outside this fixed block supplied. No cross-entry or cross-reader borrowing.

rubric.correct: Every actually requested fact correct, resolved and summary-supported; equivalent complete meaning accepted; no material contradiction.
rubric.partial: Missing/unresolved requested fact with no material contradiction.
rubric.incorrect: Any material contradiction, including volunteered contextual claims.

global_constraints: No borrowing a fact from another question or reader.
Do not require ancillary source-only facts or contextual key facts excluded here.
Named board order may convey an order without listing every suit.
A clear operational equivalent passes without parroting key wording.
Semantic relation must be present: one user is not once total; paid use is not necessarily user pays; global three Visions is not personal draws; one unmatched site card is not all unmatched.
Free Chronicle together with affirmative Exile-winner permission may convey normal-offer waiver.
This file does not certify source audit or silently fix a fixed expected answer.

questions.question: Can an Exile holding an unrevealed true Vision win at Wake, or reveal it at Wake to win immediately? What if fewer than three world Visions have been drawn?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No:must already have revealed and complete at victory check;normal reveal minor action in Act,not Wake. Fewer than three world Visions blocks Visionary even if goal assets met;may reveal earlier for future.

required_facts.expected_fact: Cannot win unrevealed; must already reveal and meet goal at win check. Normal reveal is minor action in Act, not Wake.
Blocks Visionary even if goal assets met.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Separate early-reveal permission is context to the asked present victory restriction; no contrary ban may be asserted.

questions.question: Can an Exile whose title has not yet flipped to Usurper win as Oathkeeper at end of round eight? If not, who can win instead?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Oathkeeper alone not Usurper win;priority Empire-Oathkeeper absent if Exile holds,then existing Usurper,then qualifying Visionary,then Empire fallback with possible Successor. Exile can still win qualifying revealed Vision.

required_facts.expected_fact: Not a Usurper win; Exile holding title does not trigger Empire-Oathkeeper tier.
Qualifying revealed Exile Vision may win; otherwise Empire fallback with possible Citizen Successor.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Existing-Usurper branch of general round-eight order.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: A different existing Usurper cannot coexist with the specified unflipped sole title; reciting that impossible branch is contextual, not needed for this scenario.

questions.question: At Chronicle, if Exile wins through both Usurper and Vision, must next Oath match Vision? Who may receive Chronicle Citizenship and how are accepting site garrisons replaced?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Multiple-method win chooses any Oath except current,not forced Vision match. Flip all Citizen boards Exile;winner may offer other Exiles except just-flipped former Citizens,not self. Accepting Exile sites replace all garrisons with one winner-color warband per ruled site;no normal Reliquary gift.

required_facts.expected_fact: Multiple methods: any Oath except current, not forced matching Vision.
Flip all Citizens Exile; may offer other Exiles except just-flipped, not winner self.
Replace all garrisons at accepted Exile’s ruled sites with one winner-color warband per site.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: This narrow question asks who receives and garrison replacement, not offer payment; full turnover/waiver requirement in Q020 does not automatically expand Q075.

questions.question: When playing through People’s Favor, must discarded and receiving sites be identical, can the discard come from another region, and can a locked card be discarded?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Sites may differ but both must be in pawn region;cannot use power to discard elsewhere. Locked faceup card cannot be discarded. Receiving site capacity still applies;gain played-card suit favor as normal.

required_facts.expected_fact: Discarded and receiving sites may differ, both in pawn region.
Cannot discard outside pawn region through this power; cannot discard locked faceup card.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Receiving site capacity and ordinary site-play favor.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Unchanged full card-play procedure is context to the asked two-site/region/lock restrictions.

questions.question: If a victorious attacker targeted pawn/favor and a banner, must they banish, must they burn favor, and must they take the banner? What is the rounding of board favor burn?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Banish optional;board favor burn independently optional,half rounded down. Taking all targeted relics/banners mandatory. Seized banner burns two its resources min one separately from optional board-favor burn.

required_facts.expected_fact: Banish optional; board-favor burn independently optional.
Must take all targeted relics/banners.
Board burn is half rounded down.
Seized-banner two-resource burn to minimum one is separate from optional board-favor burn.

questions.question: What do skulls do if you chose fewer attack dice than board warbands, and can you sacrifice more than required to win to reduce your upkeep?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Each skull kills own force warband immediately,not one per rolled die necessarily nor defender. Choice of fewer dice does not shrink force to those dice for casualties. Sacrifice exactly necessary to win if choose,never surplus to adjust upkeep.

required_facts.expected_fact: Each skull immediately kills one own force warband; choosing fewer dice does not reduce force to rolled-die count for casualties.
If sacrificing, exactly enough to win, never surplus for upkeep.

questions.question: What does the Exile/Chancellor Supply refresh depend on exactly, and how much Supply do their personal-bank brackets give before saving?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Unused personal-bank warbands,not board/map. Chancellor 18+:6,11–17:5,4–10:4,0–3:3. Exile9+:6,4–8:5,0–3:4. Add saved remaining Supply capped at full seven. Citizen instead exact Chancellor marker.

required_facts.expected_fact: Unused personal-bank warbands, not board/map.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question explicitly asks refresh before saving, not save procedure.
Question specifically asks Exile/Chancellor, not Citizen refresh.

questions.question: Which battle-plan box colors can attacker and defender use? Does rule alone permit a side to use the wrong-color plan?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Red attacker only,blue defender only,gradient either. Must rule and meet color/role permission;rule alone insufficient.

required_facts.expected_fact: Red attacker only, blue defender only, gradient either.
Must rule and meet role/color permission; rule alone cannot authorize wrong role.

questions.question: For Chancellor/Citizen versus Exile, who is an enemy? How does an intra-Empire Campaign and the phrase your enemy change that?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Ordinary Imperials enemies are Exiles;Exiles enemies any other player. Specified Citizen temporarily non-Imperial during intra-Empire Campaign considers others enemies. Bandits enemies everyone and vice versa. Your enemy means opposing Campaign side: defender+Allies for attacker,attacker for defender.
questions.source_references: Law Glossary Enemy,Your Enemy; Errata Enemy/You

required_facts.expected_fact: Imperials’ enemies are Exiles; Exiles’ enemies any other player; bandits enemies to all and vice versa.
Specified temporarily non-Imperial Citizen treats other players as enemies, not all Citizens globally changed.
Opposing Campaign side: defender+Allies for attacker; attacker for defending side.

questions.question: May Search voluntarily draw only one of three available cards when no Vision or reducing modifier intervenes? What if source runs out?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No;draw prescribed three unless world Vision stops,source exhausted,or applicable modifier changes count. Empty source means take only available,no automatic reshuffle.

required_facts.expected_fact: No; prescribed three unless world Vision stop, depletion or applicable modifier.
Take only available cards; no automatic reshuffle.

questions.question: At setup, where do the Round and Visions Drawn markers start? Who takes the first turn of every round, in which direction does play proceed, what phases make a turn, and when is an end-of-round victory check made relative to moving the round marker?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Both markers start on their first/star spaces (Round1 and Visions Drawn0). Starting with the Chancellor each round, go clockwise with one turn per player. Each turn is Wake, Act, Rest in that order. After every player has taken a turn, the round ends: check the applicable end-of-round victory condition before advancing the round marker; round8 ends automatically.
questions.source_references: Law 1.2; Law 4 introductory paragraph; Law 3.3–4; Playbook p6 step5; Playbook p10

required_facts.expected_fact: Round first/star space1; Visions Drawn first/star space0.
Chancellor first each round, clockwise one turn each; Wake→Act→Rest.
After all players turn, check round-end victory before advancing round marker; round eight ends automatically.

questions.question: During the first-game packet setup, do players make the later-game bottom-deck adviser draws or shuffle the ordered packet world deck? How are the regional discards and the Reliquary/relic deck prepared?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Use the assigned facedown advisers instead of later-game adviser draws. Put three facedown cards in the Cradle discard, three in the Provinces discard and five in the Hinterland discard. Put the remaining41 denizen/Vision cards on the World Deck space in Packet B order. Give the Chancellor the Grand Scepter, put Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain, put the next four relic cards facedown in the four Reliquary spaces, and the remaining15 on the Relic Deck space. Preserve the packet instructions/order rather than replacing this with later setup’s bottom draws and random preparation.
questions.source_references: Playbook p7 steps12–18; Playbook p6–7 first-game setup; Law 1 introductory first-time exception

required_facts.expected_fact: Use assigned facedown advisers, not later bottom draws; preserve ordered Packet B world deck.
Three Cradle, three Provinces, five Hinterland facedown; remaining41 denizen/Vision cards in Packet B order on world deck.
Ivory Eye facedown Mountain; next four relics facedown one per Reliquary space; remaining15 relic deck, preserving packet order.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Separate player-held setup item, not regional/world/Relic deck or Reliquary preparation asked here.

questions.question: Before resolving the first game’s Chronicle, how must the unopened Archive Packet be prepared?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Open the Archive Packet. Put the eight cardboard separators in the small box compartment. Put the six edifices in their matching-suit sections. Shuffle each of the six suit stacks separately and put each stack in its matching section; this forms the Archive. Then use the Chronicle aid and Law8 to pack/save the game.
questions.source_references: Playbook p29 Ending Your First Game

required_facts.expected_fact: Open; put eight separators in small box compartment.
Put six edifices in matching-suit sections.
Shuffle each of six suit stacks separately into matching section to form Archive.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Then follow Chronicle aid/Law8 to pack/save.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Subsequent Chronicle use is not preparation of the Archive Packet.

questions.question: If a power lets an Exile become a Citizen with no offer, is a Grand Scepter offer or exactly one Reliquary relic still required, and which status-conversion consequences still apply?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No. Forced Citizenship follows the power and the acceptance/conversion procedure in6.6.2 without requiring the ordinary offer in6.6.1 or its promised Reliquary relic. Flip the board to Citizen, replace board/map warbands with available purple warbands with the Exile choosing shortage removals/replacements, discard a revealed Vision, flip a held Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if it is their turn, and refresh Supply to the leftmost space. Do not invent an ordinary promised exchange when there was no offer.

required_facts.expected_fact: No Scepter offer or promised Reliquary relic required; follow power and conversion, no invented promised exchange.
Flip Citizen, replace board/map with available purple with recipient choosing shortage replacements/removals.
Discard revealed Vision, held Usurper→Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full leftmost Supply.

questions.question: A normal Action/modifier card already holds favor or a secret. May you place another favor/secret on it to pay for its power? May its power still be used if it has no cost, and what special case changes the payment rule?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Normally you cannot place favor or secrets on a card that already has either, so you cannot pay such a placement cost. Occupancy does not prevent using a power that has no cost. Battle plans specifically allow placing payment on an occupied card, while still being usable only once per Campaign; this does not permit Muster or Trade on an occupied card.
questions.source_references: Law 7.1.2; Law 7.5.3; Card Reference p1 Rules of Use: Exhaustion; Playbook p32 Using Cards

required_facts.expected_fact: Cannot place favor/secrets to pay on card already holding either.
Occupancy does not prevent using no-cost power.
Battle plans permit payment on occupied card.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: General use limit not specifically asked by payment-rule question.
Other action eligibility is outside the asked normal power/payment exception.

questions.question: What mandatory defense-die bonus does the Oathkeeper title give on its Oathkeeper side versus its Usurper side? Is this a Campaign modifier, and how does Supremacy apply it to Imperial defense?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: The Oathkeeper must add one defense die; the Usurper must add two. The title bonus is a Campaign modifier. For Supremacy the Chancellor holds the title if the Empire meets the goal and always adds its power when any Imperial player defends. Apply the errata’s side-sharing permissions to participating Imperial defenders/Allies in other Oaths as well.
questions.source_references: Law 2.11; Errata Law Clarifications2.11; Errata Campaign power-sharing

required_facts.expected_fact: Oathkeeper mandatory one defense die; Usurper mandatory two; Campaign modifier.
In Supremacy, the Chancellor adds the held title's bonus when any Imperial player defends.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question asks how Supremacy applies the bonus; other-Oath extension is contextual (required in broad Q017).

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Chancellor holds the Supremacy title if the Empire collectively meets the goal.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Title allocation and goal qualification explain who normally supplies the bonus but are not independently requested by the question about bonus amounts, modifier status, and application to Imperial defense. The requirement that the held title power applies when any Imperial player defends remains in Q088-F02.

questions.question: A power says to move or swap a denizen rather than play it. Must this obey site/adviser capacities and tree/person/locked restrictions? Does the movement by itself award the favor for playing to a site or trigger a When Played power?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Move follows capacity, play-placement and restriction rules (2.8.1,5.1.4,7.2); Swap moves both prompted pieces to each other’s locations and also follows those movement rules. A move/swap is not itself a play, so it does not by itself award the favor for playing to a site or trigger When Played. A power explicitly saying to play follows the Play rules and those triggers.
questions.source_references: Law Glossary Move,Swap,Play; Law 9.1 literal interpretation; Law 5.1.4.I; Law 7.3.3

required_facts.expected_fact: Obey site/adviser capacities, placement and tree/person/locked restrictions; Swap moves both pieces to each other’s locations under those rules.
Movement alone is not Play: no site-play favor or When Played trigger.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: If effect explicitly says Play, follow normal play triggers.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Different hypothetical instruction is context; no need to restate all rules for it.

questions.question: When a Citizen’s purple warband is killed by a skull, sacrifice, or Campaign loss, which bank receives it? How does this differ from moving a defeated force’s surviving warbands?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Kill moves a warband to the personal bank of the player of that color: purple goes to the Chancellor’s personal bank even when killed from a Citizen’s board. Sacrifice means choosing to kill one’s own warband. Defeated survivors move to a board rather than to a personal bank; in Imperial defense surviving site warbands go to the Chancellor’s board and survivors already on Citizen boards stay there.
questions.source_references: Law Glossary Kill,Sacrifice; Law 5.5.5–6; Law 5.5.7.I Empire box as relocated by errata

required_facts.expected_fact: Purple always Chancellor personal bank, whether skull/sacrifice/loss from Citizen board.
Defeated survivors move to board, not bank; Imperial site survivors Chancellor board, Citizen-board survivors stay there.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Sacrifice definition as choosing own kill.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Terminology definition is context to the asked killed-piece destination, not a separate requested explanation.
